comparisons.peer_summary: AMD was the first company to integrate a dedicated neural processing unit (NPU) on the same SoC as an x86 CPU for AI PCs.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron disclose the integration of specific AI processing hardware into PC architectures to support next-generation AI workloads. While Micron focuses on the memory subsystem requirements (higher DRAM content and low-power modules) necessitated by these chipsets, AMD highlights its provision of the processing silicon itself, specifically the integration of a neural processing unit (NPU) directly on the System-on-Chip (SoC) alongside the CPU.

sentences.text: The next generation PCs that have been announced contain high-performance neural processing chipsets as well as AI.

In 2024, we announced the low-power compression-attached memory module to deliver the required performance to process AI workloads on PCs and provide the potential to scale to applications needing a high performance and low power solution in a compact and modular form factor.
AMD was the first company to integrate a dedicated neural processing unit (NPU) on the same SoC as an x86 CPU for AI PCs.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel views AI as a generational shift and aims to bring AI to where data is generated and used, addressing the full AI continuum from GenAI to AI PCs and edge computing. The company leverages a spectrum of hardware and software platforms for open, modular solutions and is infusing AI into its technologies to support current and future workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron identify 'AI PCs' as a key emerging usage and growth driver for their respective technologies. Micron explicitly links the rise of AI PCs to a demand for 'significantly more DRAM content,' whereas Intel describes 'AI PCs' as an emerging usage phase of the AI continuum where the company is infusing AI into its technologies to support such local workloads.

sentences.text: PC: Our products sold to the client PC market support both commercial and consumer PC unit growth.
We expect these devices will have significantly more DRAM content than today's average PC.
We also seek to address every phase of the AI continuum, from the largest, most challenging GenAI and large language models to emerging usages like AI PCs and AI at the edge.

We are infusing AI into Intel technologies, supporting today's GenAI workloads, fueling emerging usages like AI PC and AI at the edge, and pioneering innovations that we believe will help advance the future of AI in the next decade.

comparisons.peer_summary: Gamers and creators choose NVIDIA GPUs for immersive experiences, with the market expanding due to live streamers and the advent of generative AI for local PC usage.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and Micron discuss the expansion of the PC market driven by generative AI. NVIDIA notes that users are choosing GPUs for running 'generative AI applications locally on their PC' for privacy and latency reasons, which aligns with Micron's observation that AI use cases proliferating to PCs create a need for higher-performance memory subsystems and increased DRAM content.

sentences.text: As AI use cases proliferate to PCs, performance of the memory subsystem becomes more critical.
We expect these devices will have significantly more DRAM content than today's average PC.

With the advent of generative AI, we expect a broader set of PC users to choose NVIDIA GPUs for running generative AI applications locally on their PC, which is critical for privacy, latency, and cost-sensitive AI applications.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consumer IoT products are adopting latest mobile connectivity and on-device AI capabilities, with new AI-focused PCs launching in 2024 and analysts expecting 50% of PCs sold to be AI capable by 2027.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Micron identify the launch of AI-focused PCs in 2024 and the adoption of on-device AI capabilities as a key market trend. Qualcomm highlights the launch of Snapdragon X Series AI PCs and expects 50% of PCs to be AI-capable by 2027, while Micron confirms that next-generation PCs with AI capabilities contain 'significantly more DRAM content than today's average PC.'

sentences.text: The next generation PCs that have been announced contain high-performance neural processing chipsets as well as AI.
We expect these devices will have significantly more DRAM content than today's average PC.

For example, a new class of AI-focused PCs, including those powered by our Snapdragon X Series platforms, launched in 2024, allowing for increased productivity and enhanced use cases enabled by on-device AI processing at low power.
By 2027, analysts expect that at least 50% of PCs sold will be AI capable, compared to 22% of PCs in 2024 (consensus of certain third party analysts as of October 1, 2024).
